title: What teachers did for him
summary: Teachers were a crutch and an intellectual force.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I think we've gotten pretty rigid ideas of what educating really is and to most people it means sitting in a classroom and grading papers.
The best education I've gotten from teachers have been in other ways.

It's being lead into some strange direction you never really thought was there, and you found it worked for you. I never really learned anything from teachers, it's just that they were a crutch, a necessary crutch at the time, at least with me (inaudible). I never really learned anything from him but it forced me to look certain ways by myself, so that way he was good. They didn't really help me as far as putting notes on paper. It's just that they were an intellectual force that caused me to exercise a part of my brain that would not be
exercised if I weren't involved with them.
It's not necessarily a fault, maybe it's a characteristic. You don't have to take it negatively.
Well, I know other people who had become quite prolific composers because they (inaudible), and I've been accused of being prolific in the right situation.

When the situation arises, I have to stop and think about where I am and what I'm doing and then I freeze. I can't write for a closet. I can write if somebody needs it; need is probably the basis of it. It there is a need I'll do it, but if not, I diddle.
